newsitem.title: USA: Surgeons remove half of brains to stop seizures.
newsitem.headline: Surgeons remove half of brains to stop seizures.

text.p: Radical surgery removing half the brains of children afflicted with severe seizures quieted the electrical misfires in the remaining half and allowed them to lead more normal lives, researchers said on Friday.
Writing in the journal Pediatrics, surgeons from the Johns Hopkins Medical Institutions in Baltimore summarized their findings from 58 such hemispherectomies performed over three decades.

Of 54 surviving children, surgery was declared very successful for 44 of them, and 29 were seizure-free. Another seven surgeries were termed moderately successful, and three were said to be minimally successful.

Surgeons Sumio Uematsu and Benjamin Carson, co-authors of the journal article, speculated that a severely malfunctioning brain hemisphere, found in some victims of Rasmussen's Syndrome and dysplasias, can electrically interfere with the healthier half of the brain.
"This might explain why motor function improves after hemispherectomy and why language recovers after removal of the dysfunctional left hemisphere," they wrote.
After infancy, the younger an afflicted child undergoes the operation the greater likelihood of success, they said.

"We are awed by the apparent retention of memory after removal of half of the brain, either half, and by the retention of the child's personality and sense of humour. Yet we look forward to the time when there are less mutilating approaches to these problems," they wrote.
